newsitem.title: UK: Sugar freight market busy with fixed, new business.
newsitem.headline: Sugar freight market busy with fixed, new business.

text.p: The sugar freight market saw an upturn in its fortunes on Thursday with a spate of fixtures and new orders from a variety of origins, shipbrokers said.
They said the rate achieved on the fixture recently reported for Mauritius Sugar Syndicate's 14,500 tonnes of bulk sugar from Port Louis to London was stg 13.95.
Cargill entered the market with a new order for 14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Poland to Syria with options of Egypt and Tunisia for 9/13 December.

Scanports quoted for 12,500 tonnes of bagged sugar from Puerto Quetzal to Chile for end December/early January and Seven Seas was open for a 14,000-tonne bagged cargo from south Brazil to Red Sea or East Africa.

Booker was open for 8/10,000 tonnes in bags on its usual run from Georgeton to UK/Nantes for 12/17 December and Czarnikow Rionda was looking for a vessel to ship a prompt 12/13,000-tonne bagged cargo from north Brazil to Red Sea/East Africa.

Jean Lion quoted for 16/18,000 tonnes in bulk from Cuba to the Black Sea for end December and was said to have fixed 14,000 tonnes from north Brazil to Syria for December dates. Other fixtures included Genoc, said to have covered its earlier prompt order for 12/14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from south Brazil to Mediterranean with options of Black Sea, Red Sea and Indian Ocean.

Shipbrokers said Amerop fixed 24,500 tonnes of bulk sugar from Salaverry to US Gulf/Atlantic for 17/24 December. Genoc revised its earlier order for 14,000 tonnes in bulk from Cuba to Mediterranean/Black Sea for end December and also quoted for 7,500/8,700 tonnes from Salaverry to US Gulf/Atlantic for 23 December/5 January. Elsewhere, Tunisia bought one cargo of white sugar from a London trade house for August shipment.
